edits.find: - **Reopened.** The runtime authoring surface, [issue #223](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/issues/223). Every slice from A1 to F landed, and then a re-review of the whole run against `0bb854e` found four things that did not land with them. Three of them are closed now: the immediate-verb refusal, which was the one defect among them; the duplicate reverse-topology derivation in `dependantsOf`; and the authoring-side cost that none of the seven tick-side optimisations reached, in two slices, one for the document a commit builds and one for what it writes and what an authored read derives. What is left is one unverified premise behind the empty flush seed on a removal, and it is a measurement before it is a change. This file said the issue was closed with nothing open in it while the issue was open, and on the first finding the file was what was wrong rather than the state.
edits.replace:
- **Closed, on the state rather than ahead of it.** The runtime authoring surface, [issue #223](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/issues/223). Every slice from A1 to F landed, then a re-review of the whole run against `0bb854e` found four things that did not land with them, and all four are closed now: the immediate-verb refusal, which was the one defect the re-review was willing to call one; the duplicate reverse-topology derivation in `dependantsOf`; the authoring-side cost that none of the seven tick-side optimisations reached, priced per motion, per op and per access; and the flush a removal owes the nodes that were reading it. This file once said the issue was closed with nothing open in it while the issue was open, and on the first finding the file was what was wrong rather than the state.
- **Just landed.** The flush a removal owes the nodes that were reading it, which is the fourth finding and the one the re-review would not take on the docblock's word. `touched` was empty for a removal because `SchemaCommit` said the removed node was gone with nothing left depending on it, and `finalizeGraph` would have refused the candidate otherwise. Half of that holds: the edge walk in `finalizeGraph` covers every edge of every node rather than only the observation ones, so a plugin requirement naming a removed source is refused before anything commits, which is what `RA-98` pins. The other half does not, and it is finding 2's asymmetry one member over: a solver reads its chain members through `solves`, no edge points that way, and under the bare goal slot a chain that loses its leaf still has exactly one, so every rule passes, the commit lands, the solver's member set moves and nothing publishes. A removal now seeds the nodes that were reading the removed one, read from the same `GraphIR.dependents` the public query reads. `RA-98` and `RA-99` are its evidence, and it earns no ADR: the premise lived in one docblock and one line of this file and nowhere else.
- **The decision worth carrying forward from it.** One question keeps one owner even when its two consumers are a public preflight and a private derivation. `#readersOf` is that owner and `dependantsOf` is a projection of it, because the alternatives are both the defect this issue has already paid for once: `#derive` reading `dependents` itself is a second derivation of the fact finding 2 unified, and `#derive` calling the public member instead binds a commit's own invariant to a preflight's contract and points the dependency at this class's surface rather than away from it. Passing the answer in as a third parameter was refused for a smaller reason: `#derive` already reads the retained pair off the class under the same ordering rule, so a parameter for one of two identically ordered reads would claim the two are different.

edits.find: An add, a replacement and every authored edit seed the edited node; a motion add or destroy and a removal seed nothing, because the first two derive no node at all and a removal's node is gone with nothing left depending on it.
edits.replace: An add, a replacement and every authored edit seed the edited node; a motion add or destroy seeds nothing, because neither derives a node at all; and a removal seeds the nodes that were reading the removed one, which is empty for most removals and is not the same claim as seeding nothing. `finalizeGraph` refuses a candidate whose removed node is still named by an edge, so that reader never reaches the seed, but a solver reads its chain members through `solves` with no edge pointing that way and that candidate is accepted, so the readers are read off the graph the removal is replacing, before it is replaced.

edits.find: - An audit's claim about callers is a measurement, not a premise.
edits.replace:
- A justification is held to the same rule as a claim. `touched` was empty for a removal because a docblock said `finalizeGraph` would have refused any candidate something still depended on, which is true of every reader that is an edge and false of the one reader that is not, and the sentence was written by a slice that did not change the file it was about. A comment carrying the reason a step is skipped is load-bearing: it is measured where it is written, or the skip is unproven.
- An audit's claim about callers is a measurement, not a premise.

edits.replace:
- The document a commit hands the graph: `RA-89` through `RA-91` in `packages/core/test/unit/runtime/snapshot-one-walk.test.ts`. One of three red, on assertions, with `RA-90` and `RA-91` green on purpose because they are the equivalence half and bucketing one walk may not move the document the per-motion filter produced. `RA-89` is counted rather than timed, through a prototype instrument narrowed to the one explicit `Map.prototype.entries` call in `packages/core/src`, and it reads the cost as a difference between two rigs holding the same tracks rather than as a total. The red and green run ids live in the pull request body.
- What a removal owes the nodes that read it: `RA-98` and `RA-99` in `packages/core/test/unit/runtime/removal-flush-seed.test.ts`. One of two red, on the seed assertion and on nothing else, with `RA-98` green on purpose as the accepting control: it is the half of the premise that holds, so what it states is what a removal deliberately does not owe. The other four assertions of `RA-99` are the finding rather than the fix and passed on the red run, which is what makes the case a measurement of the seed rather than of the rig. The red and green run ids live in the pull request body, and so does the run before them that is not evidence: the case read a removed node through the resolver rather than through the probe, so it threw before reaching the assertion it exists for.
- Every earlier slice's red and green run ids live in the pull request that landed it.
